required_fixes: Implement actual brotli/gzip compression in MockOAuthHandler: inspect Accept-Encoding (or force per-baseline encoding), compress body via brotli.compress(data, quality=q) for q in [4,5,6,7,8] and gzip.compress, set Content-Encoding header to 'br'/'gzip' or omit for identity, and set Content-Length to compressed length. Current handler at research/experiments/EXP-RUNTIME-35154720995/run_experiment.py:260-301 never sets Content-Encoding and always sends raw body (raw_observations.json content_encoding='none' 2880/2880, body_hash_compressed == decompressed_hash 2880/2880). Without compressed wire bytes, decompression-normalization branch in decompress_body() (lines 340-353) is never exercised (identity fallback only).

Re-run baselines so that DECOMPRESSED-VARYING-BROTLI and DECOMPRESSED-VARYING-GZIP are distinct compressed streams whose decompressed bodies can be compared. Currently both baselines send identical uncompressed bytes (fingerprints identical 2880/2880, |brotli-gzip|=0.0 vacuous, compressed_hash_variation unique_count=1 in all 36 metric cells). Verification must show Content-Encoding in {br,gzip,identity}, body_size reduced vs uncompressed target (e.g., 1016 -> ~30-70B for error bodies at gzip/brotli), and decompressed_hash derived via brotli.decompress/gzip.decompress matches uncompressed sha.

Fix measurement_validity and claim scope to match implementation: either (a) re-execute under real compression and re-evaluate decision_rule (including falsifier OR brotli quality diversity does not increase), or (b) downgrade claim to 'status+body hash discrimination under identity (no compression) for synthetic JSON/HTML/XML at 1KB/10KB/100KB' and explicitly state decompression-normalization was NOT tested. Current report.md Section 3.5-3.6 and Section 7 claim 'under localhost compression' and 'decompression latency <0.1ms' are not supported (latency 0.0004-0.0013ms measured on identity path, not on 100KB brotli decompress).

Align falsifier and decision_rule: spec.json falsifier includes 'OR brotli quality diversity does not increase from 1KB to 100KB' which IS observed (avg_diversity_1KB=1.0, avg_diversity_100KB=1.0, C_BROTLI_QUALITY_SCALING pass=false) but decision_rule omits this condition and report declares SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST. Required: either include quality-scaling in decision_rule and report FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING for quality-diversity, or remove it from falsifier and disclose that brotli quality convergence for small compressible payloads was not the falsifier. Do not silently ignore one of three frozen falsifier disjuncts.

validity_findings.finding: No compression was applied. All 2880 observations have Content-Encoding='none' (compression_verification content_encoding_values=['none'] in every metric cell, raw_observations.json headers only Server/Date/Content-Type/Content-Length, zero br/gzip). body_hash_compressed == decompressed_hash for 2880/2880, fingerprint_compressed == fingerprint_decompressed 2880/2880. Server handler do_GET/do_POST (run_experiment.py:260-301) never compresses, never sets Content-Encoding, always sends raw body. Defined compress_gzip/compress_brotli utilities (lines 329-338) and decompress_body() (340-353) are dead code. The question 'under brotli/gzip compression without CDN noise' and measurement_validity item 3 ('Compression uses brotli quality 4-8 and gzip') were not instantiated; the environment could not express the tested effect.

validity_findings.impact: Decompression-normalization mechanism (SHA256 on decompressed body + status via brotli.decompress/gzip.decompress after Content-Encoding inspection) was not exercised. Reported decompressed_body_only_discrimination 0.5 equals compressed_body_only_discrimination 0.5 trivially, not due to normalization. Status COMPLETE is incorrect; should be MEASUREMENT_INVALID per spec 'MEASUREMENT_INVALID if infrastructure failure prevents valid measurements'.

validity_findings.finding: Baseline B-ALGORITHM-EQUIVALENCE |brotli - gzip| <0.1 reported as 0.0 PASS for all 18 content_type x size pairs, but both baselines are the same uncompressed stream relabeled DECOMPRESSED-VARYING-BROTLI vs GZIP. With no compression, algorithm invariance is tautologically true. Parent EXP-RUNTIME-35137033384 produced 3 Content-Encoding types (br/gzip/identity) and distinct compressed hashes (2-4 uniques), providing a meaningful test; this experiment collapsed to 1 unique for both algorithms.

validity_findings.finding: Control C_BROTLI_QUALITY_SCALING fails as observed (avg 1.0 at 1KB and 100KB, pass=false, Falsifier third disjunct TRUE) but is reported as benign. However with no compression, unique_count=1 is not 'brotli qualities 4-8 converge for small compressible payloads' but 'no compression applied, so quality irrelevant'. Falsifier states decompression discrimination <0.3 OR decompressed variation >1 OR brotli diversity does not increase -> hypothesis falsified on third disjunct. Producer ignores falsifier and still declares SURVIVES because decision_rule omitted that clause, creating a frozen inconsistency between spec falsifier and decision_rule.

validity_findings.impact: Interpretation overstates 'mechanism is size-invariant'; the size-dependent brotli diversity hypothesis is actually falsified under the no-compression implementation, but the result is uninformative about real compressibility scaling (which would require compressible vs random payloads at 10KB/100KB producing size-dependent compressed sizes).

validity_findings.finding: Positive control C_DECOMPRESSION_DETERMINISM all_same=true for all 36 conditions (144 state cells) is reported as confirming mechanism determinism. Since decompression path is identity (no Content-Encoding), determinism is trivial (hashing same raw bytes). Real test would require varying compressed bytes per state (different qualities producing different wire bytes) that decompress to one body (unique decompressed 1, compressed >1). Current decompressed_hash_variation and compressed_hash_variation are both 1, so no evidence that brotli.decompress correctly inverts multiple quality variants.
validity_findings.evidence_ref: research/experiments/EXP-RUNTIME-35154720995/result.json metrics decompressed_hash_variation all_same true 144/144 and compressed_hash_variation all_same true 144/144; raw_observations.json decompressed_hash == body_hash_compressed 2880/2880; report.md Section 3.3 'fully deterministic'
validity_findings.impact: SURVIVES condition (4) passes vacuously. Cannot extrapolate that decompression is deterministic under CDN brotli quality variation (parent had 2-4 compressed uniques collapsing to 1 decompressed, showing real normalization).

validity_findings.finding: Report.md Section 3.7 claims decompression latency mean ~0.001ms at 1KB, ~0.003ms at 10KB, ~0.025ms at 100KB with assessment '<0.1ms even at 100KB, cost negligible'. Recomputed decompression_latency_ms in result.json is actually 0.00062ms mean at 1KB (min 0.00041 max 0.00128), 0.00082-0.00117ms at 10KB, 0.00076-0.00081ms at 100KB — essentially timing of identity branch return, not brotli/gzip decompress of 10-100KB. Real 100KB brotli decompress latency would be higher (parent not measured but system brotli library expected ~0.02-0.1ms).

validity_findings.finding: Recomputed decompressed discrimination =0.5 for all 18 /userinfo cells and 0.5 for all 18 /introspect cells (status_only 0.5 /userinfo, 0.0 /introspect) correctly reflects 3-way error collapse (no_auth/expired/invalid identical bodies, valid distinct). This equals structural ceiling and matches B-PARENT-JSON-1KB expectation (0.5). However this validates only that status+body hashing distinguishes valid vs error bodies for JSON/HTML/XML at 1KB-100KB under identity encoding, not that it survives non-determinism in compressed wire bytes. Compressed discrimination also 0.5 (vs parent 0.2789 under CDN noise) because without noise compressed == decompressed.

validity_findings.impact: Result supports narrow body-content distinction, not decompression-normalization robustness. Parent ceiling (decompressed 0.5 /userinfo 0.8333 /introspect, compressed 0.2789) demonstrated CDN-induced degradation; this experiment cannot show degradation because no CDN/compression, so hypothesis that mechanism operates on decompressed logical bodies is untested.

validity_findings.finding: Three synthetic content types are structurally realistic in tag form but highly padded (repeating paragraph/list/element blocks targeting 1KB/10KB/100KB exactly: body_sizes JSON 1016/10232/102392, HTML 1024/10240/102400, XML similar). Bodies are compressible x* padding, not natural incompressible Web pages; real HTML with scripts/styles and XML with attributes would have different compressibility and brotli quality divergence. Server uses class-level body_size/content_type (run_experiment.py:225-228) which is safe here (sequential servers on BASE_PORT+idx) but race-prone if parallel. N=20 per state seeded shuffle deterministic (seed 44) — adequate for deterministic case but no power analysis for non-deterministic compressed variation.

claim_ceiling: Narrow ceiling justified: On localhost mock OAuth2 (Python BaseHTTPServer) with identity encoding only (no brotli/gzip compression, Content-Encoding 'none' 2880/2880), SHA256 on raw body + status distinguishes valid_token (200 with distinct user body) from no_auth/expired_token/invalid_token (401 with identical error body, 3-way collapse) at structural ceiling 0.5 on both /userinfo (status 0.5) and /introspect (status 0.0 -> 0.5 via body) for synthetic JSON (1016/10232/102392B), HTML (1024/10240/102400B), XML (similar) at 1KB/10KB/100KB padded sizes, N=20 per state per condition (80 per condition, 2880 total), seed 44, decompression path not exercised (identity fallback, latency ~0.0004-0.0013ms). Does NOT support: decompression-normalization (SHA256 on decompressed body via brotli.decompress/gzip.decompress) preserves discrimination under brotli/gzip compression; algorithm-equivalence of brotli vs gzip after decompression; brotli quality diversity scaling with payload size; latency cost of decompression at 10KB/100KB; or any CDN non-determinism resilience. Real compression must be implemented and re-measured before advancing claim ceiling beyond parent EXP-RUNTIME-35137033384 ('synthetic proxy + CDN simulator with realistic non-determinism' at 1KB JSON).
